note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Open seat (Sen. Peters retiring).

MI-senate.statusNote: Open seat: Abdul El-Sayed (D) won the Aug 4 primary over Haley Stevens; Mike Rogers (R) is the Republican nominee.

MI-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Whitmer term-limited): Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson (D) faces Rep. John James (R), both nominated Aug 4.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.background: Physician and epidemiologist; former Detroit health director and Wayne County health official; author of 'Medicare for All: A Citizen's Guide.' Won the August 2026 Democratic primary.

cost.label: Union member (SEIU/AFT/UAW); campaigns on expanding union protections and worker power (Wikipedia)

health.label: Supports Medicare for All; co-wrote a book on it (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Backed repealing state preemption of rent control (2018) (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Supports abolishing ICE while keeping 'certain kinds' of border enforcement (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 100% renewable energy by 2030; tougher environmental enforcement (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: 'A billionaire tax on wealth over $1 billion,' tax capital gains over $1M as ordinary income, close the stepped-up basis loophole and Social Security cap (Abdul for Senate)

education.label: 'I oppose efforts to privatize public education through vouchers'; $60,000 minimum teacher salary; universal pre-K (Abdul for Senate)

safety.label: 2020: invest in 'any and all efforts to get people out of jails and prisons,' policing as 'duct tape' for broken systems; later deleted defund-police posts (Fox News)

repro.label: 'Unwavering in his support for reproductive rights for women'; vows to reverse the erosion of these rights (Abdul for Senate)

democracy.label: Automatic registration at 18, 'no-reason absentee and early in-person voting,' opposes 'mandatory Voter ID laws like the SAVE Act' (Abdul for Senate)

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.background: Former FBI special agent and U.S. Representative (2001–2015), chaired the House Intelligence Committee; 2024 Senate nominee, running again in 2026.

cost.label: Argues controlling federal spending and rates, not intervention, lowers costs (Wikipedia)

health.label: Voted repeatedly against Medicare drug-price negotiation; opposes ACA provisions, favors free-market care (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Backs border wall and stricter enforcement; blames 'open borders' for crime (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Emphasizes cutting federal spending; backs Trump tariff plans (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Former FBI agent (organized crime); campaigns on tougher enforcement (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Says he won't try to overturn Michigan's 2022 abortion-rights amendment; leaves issue to states (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Backs aggressive election-security measures incl. police monitoring of election workers; promoted 2020 fraud claims (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Housing plan 'breaks down barriers to homeownership by rolling back overregulation,' cuts red tape, tax-free new construction zones (Rogers for Senate)

education.label: Campaign pledge: 'prioritizing education not indoctrination' to set kids up for success (Rogers for Senate)

climate.label: Voted no on the 2009 Waxman-Markey cap-and-trade bill (roll call 477) and yes to approve the Keystone XL pipeline in 2014 (House Clerk roll calls)

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
candidates.background: Michigan Secretary of State since 2019; former law school dean. Awarded the JFK Profile in Courage Award for defending the 2020 election.

repro.label: Launched campaign on the Roe anniversary, signaling abortion rights as a priority (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: SoS record: Election Day registration, absentee applications to all voters, ballot tracking (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Mixed: 'streamlining regulations that slow down construction' and 'government is showing up everywhere we don't need it,' alongside cracking down on corporate investors and drug pricing (Benson for Governor)

health.label: Healthcare 'a right, not a privilege': Prescription Drug Affordability Board to approve price increases, surprise-billing ban, medical debt relief (Benson for Governor)

housing.label: Mixed: remove 'outdated zoning regulations and bureaucratic red tape' to build faster, while targeting 'Wall Street landlords' buying up homes (Benson for Governor)

climate.label: 'Clean, renewable energy is the cheapest form of energy'; invest in clean energy and manufacturing, hold 'polluters accountable' (Benson for Governor)

education.label: Daughter of two public school teachers: 'it's really critical to me... that we improve our public education system' (Michigan Public)

immigration.label: Pledged 'every tool in her toolbox' to keep federal immigration agents out of Michigan schools (Bridge Michigan)

nullNotes.taxes: checked affordability page: only a $5,000 caregiver tax credit, which does not fit the axis; no corporate raise or across-the-board cut documented; roll-call/record search also empty
nullNotes.safety: checked jocelynbenson.com issues pages, Ballotpedia, and Michigan Public interview (only a general school-safety remark), nothing documented

candidates.name: John James
candidates.background: U.S. Representative (MI-10) since 2023; West Point graduate, Apache pilot, and auto-logistics executive. Won the Aug 4 Republican primary.

health.label: Calls the ACA 'a monstrosity'; opposes it (with replacement) (Wikipedia)

education.label: Top priority: more power for parents and teachers (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Strongly pro-life; compared Roe to 'genocide'; defund Planned Parenthood (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Challenged the certification of the 2020 election results (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Voted yes on the One Big Beautiful Bill making the 2017 tax cuts permanent: 'protects the average taxpayer from a 22 percent tax hike' (james.house.gov)

immigration.label: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill and touts that it 'strengthens border security' with $46.5 billion for border barrier construction (james.house.gov)

cost.label: Voted yes on S.J.Res. 18 to repeal the CFPB's $5 overdraft fee cap, April 9, 2025 (House Clerk roll call 96)

climate.label: Voted for H.R. 1, Lower Energy Costs Act, expanding fossil fuel production and fast-tracking permitting, March 30, 2023 (House Clerk roll call 182)

nullNotes.housing: checked Spectrum News interview, james.house.gov, and Ballotpedia, nothing documented; roll-call/record search also empty
